### Problem

On a multi-user Music Assistant server (tested on 2.9.9), the **frontend/UI language** can only be set:

- per user (stored server-side in the user's `preferences.language`), or
- per browser (`localStorage["frontend.settings.language"]`),

with the effective default being `"auto"` → `navigator.language`.

There is a server-level **metadata** language (`core.metadata` → *Preferred language*), but that only affects fetched metadata (descriptions/artwork), **not** the UI.

There is currently **no way for an admin to set a default UI language for the whole instance** — applied to newly created users and used as the fallback instead of `auto`. In a household/organization where everyone should get the same non-English UI by default (e.g. French), the admin has to set it manually for each user, and any newly created user falls back to browser-based `auto`.

### Requested feature

A **core/server setting for the default frontend UI language** (e.g. under Settings → Core) that:

- is used as the default for newly created users, and
- acts as the fallback when a user hasn't explicitly chosen a language (instead of `auto`),

while still letting each user override it (English/oth
posts.title: Server-level default UI (frontend) language setting

posts.excerpt:
### Problem

The Smart Playlist "Year" rule filters using the release year stored for the
album/track, which for compilations, "best of" albums, and reissues is the
reissue date — not the original recording/release year. This makes
decade-based smart playlists (e.g. "90s hits") unreliable for anything in
your library via a compilation.

Example: "Come Softly To Me" by The Fleetwoods, originally released in 1959
(Capitol Records), is in my library via the compilation "Come Softly To Me:
The Very Best Of The Fleetwoods" (1992, via Qobuz). A Smart Playlist rule
"Year: 1990-2000" picks it up, even though it's a 1959 track.

### Proposed solution

Add support for an "original release year" field (distinct from the
edition/compilation year) that the Smart Playlist Year filter can use when
available from the provider/metadata — similar to the year vs.
original_year distinction used by beets/MusicBrainz Picard.

### Alternatives considered

None that I know of within MA itself — happy to hear if there's already a
workaround.
posts.title: Smart Playlist "Year" filter: use original recording year, not reissue/compilation year

Music Assistant has been gathering quite a lot of data about artists and associated images.
The recently 'Music Quiz' plug-in made me realise that there is a lot of untapped potential.

Amazon Prime has a feature called 'X-ray' that showcases trivia about the scenes you are watching (often the actors in a given scene).
I rarely use it, because well ... I'm watching a movie so I don't want to be annoyed with silly trivia.

Listening to music is different.
There's this big empty canvas that is asking to be filled with (optional) bits.
We can already choose to look at lyrics (with the Party mode giving those their place to shine) and queue (boring, but useful).

But what about a randomised trivia section ?
Surely there's more trivia to be found beyond the 'boring' artist/band biography ?
It could help prepare you for the music quiz by displaying bits of trivia about either track, album or artist.
For tracks that have composer and individual band members listed there is even more  to explore.

**Problem**

Music Assistant never expires player registrations. When a client device re-registers under a new id — app reinstall with an install-scoped id, factory reset, restored-from-backup, a client identity bug — the old entry stays in Settings → Players as "unavailable" forever. There is no TTL, no auto-hide, and no bulk cleanup: each orphan must be found and deleted one at a time.

We maintain Sendspin clients (an Android TV / Apple TV visualizer player, plus contributions to SendspinKit — e.g. Sendspin/SendspinKit#36), and a single client-side identity bug on one Apple TV produced **seven** orphaned "unavailable" copies of the same physical device on one server before anyone noticed. Cleaning that server took the player list from 66 to 48 entries, all removed one by one. We've since made our client ids reinstall-stable, but no client can prevent this class of cruft in general — factory resets alone guarantee a slow drip of orphans for every user, and every player provider (not just Sendspin) is affected.

## Problem
There's currently no easy way to share what you're listening to with another MA user. Exporting a playlist as a file works, but it's not the same as a simple "hey, check out this track" moment — it requires extra steps and the recipient still has to manually import it.

## Proposed solution
A Share button in the player (and in context menus for tracks, artists and playlists) that generates a shareable link. When someone opens the link in their own MA instance, it resolves the item against their available providers automatically — regardless of which providers they use.

The key insight: user A on Spotify and user B on Apple Music can both open the same link and find the right track, because the link uses provider-agnostic identifiers (like ISRC or MusicBrainz ID) and falls back to a simple search if needed.

## Use cases
* Share a "now playing" status in chats or on social media
* Send a track or playlist recommendation to a friend who also uses MA

## Technical note
This would work similarly to the "My Home Assistant" button — a stateless redirect link where all the item info is encoded in the URL itself. No central database or storage needed.

posts.excerpt:
I'd like to propose an API for pre-caching of music/podcasts for offline play. Current Sendspin requires a consistent and not too segmented internet connection between client and server, so it's hardly usable for spotty connections on roads and trains.

The idea is that offline-capable apps pre-cache these files to app-private storage, so it's explicitly _not_ meant to start a second music library for other apps or users to access. Rather, the cache would be used only by that app for offline play on planes, or to bridge timespans without internet, and for limited search to find such cached tracks. Apps would be aware of the canonical storage location on the server, so any metadata (playback history, listening position, favorites etc.) would still be persisted and visible to other clients, including pure Sendspin clients.

Clients of the proposed API would not necessarly get the original data. Rather, they receive a version targetted at their playback abilities, also taking into account reduced bandwidth. So the audio might be transcoded to a different codec, bit rate and/or bit depth. Volume-adjustments and other DSP workload might already be applied.

Currently, as described in a comment [here](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5849#issuecomment-4966505097), Music Assistant disallows setting higher buffer sizes on machines at certain RAM thresholds.

This is an opinionated position, but disallowing a feature on an arbitrary threshold is removing some of the freedoms of the software user who may know the compromises made in order for it to work. Before this option was removed, I had run a perfectly stable server on a setting that is now no longer available to me (and the experience is now worse because of it).

I suggest that instead of removing the option from the frontend entirely, that the other buffer sizes are offered, and a user provided an appropriate warning that it may cause stability or OOM issues in some situations, if the hardware is below certain memory thresholds.

Additionally, I suspect that these thresholds have been set too high. I outline some thoughts about this [in this follow up comment](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5849#issuecomment-4966603603) on the same original issue.
posts.title: Allow higher buffer sizes on lower memory devices

Summary

On a 4-core Intel N100 mini PC (Music Assistant 2.9, filesystem_local provider, 65,387 candidate tracks), the Sonic Analysis background scan projects 317–635 days to cover the full library (measured, not estimated — see below). For comparison, Plex's own Sonic Analysis feature completed a comparable-sized library on the same physical host in 2 weeks. That gap (roughly 10-20x) is far larger than I'd expect from "different implementation," so I dug into why.

I don't think this is a single bug — it looks like three separate, compounding design choices, all deliberate (I found a maintainer comment in #5686 confirming the CPU-only, "polite background citizen" philosophy), but I think the combination is worth reconsidering for hosts with low core counts, where the current formula lands in the worst-case bucket.

Measured baseline

- Host: 4-core Intel N100, background_scan_concurrency=2 (default for ≥4 cores)
- Run window: 489.37s (8m 9s), cancelled mid-run for measurement purposes
- Results: 21,472 tracks completed Loudness Analysis in that window (~43.9 tracks/sec), but only 7 tracks completed the full pipeline including Sonic Analysis (~1 track per ~70s aggregate a

posts.excerpt:
Hi everyone,

I would like to propose a small but significant improvement regarding the frontend localization when Music Assistant runs as a Home Assistant app.

Currently, when the Home Assistant system language is set to Serbian Latin (`sr-Latn`) and Music Assistant is set to "Auto (follow system configuration)", MA opens in Serbian Cyrillic (`sr`). While explicitly selecting Serbian Latin in MA fixes the main interface, the initial 'Authenticating...' dialog still defaults to Cyrillic.

When discussing this, it was pointed out that Music Assistant is not exclusively a Home Assistant app. I completely agree, but given that Music Assistant is a proud part of the Open Home Foundation, there should at least be strict interoperability regarding system configuration and language matching between ecosystem apps.

Could we implement a check so that when Music Assistant detects it is running inside the HA ecosystem, it accurately inherits the host's specific language variant (like distinguishing between `sr-Latn` and `sr`) instead of falling back to a general default?

Thank you for considering this and for all your great work on Music Assistant!

posts.excerpt:
### Feature request
In the album view for multi-disc albums, it would be very useful to have the option to play or add to the queue only one selected disc, instead of always playing or queueing the entire album.

### Use case
Some albums contain multiple discs, for example:

Disc 1: original album
Disc 2: bonus tracks / demos / live recordings
Disc 3: remixes or alternate versions
Currently, when viewing such an album, the main playback and queue actions apply to the whole album. In many cases, I only want to listen to one specific disc, e.g. only Disc 1 or only the bonus disc.

### Suggested behavior
In the album detail view, each disc section could have its own actions, such as:

Play this disc
Add this disc to queue
Play next
Add to playlist — optional
This could be exposed via a three-dot menu or buttons next to the disc header, for example:

Disc 1
⋮ Play / Add to queue

### Benefits

## MEDIUM · Provider/core config secrets readable by any authenticated user (missing role gate)

**CWE-862 / CWE-200.**

### Summary
`config/providers/get_value` and `config/core/get_value` are registered as API commands with **no `required_role`**, so any authenticated user — including a non-admin / guest role — can read raw config values, including `SECURE_STRING` secrets (streaming-service credentials, SSL private-key material, etc.). Mutating config commands are correctly gated to admin; the value-read path is not.

## HIGH · Reflected XSS in the OAuth callback page → session-token theft / account takeover

**CWE-79 / CWE-116.**

### Summary
`WebserverController._handle_auth_callback` builds the OAuth "Login Successful" page by string-replacing placeholders into `helpers/resources/oauth_callback.html` without any HTML/JS escaping. The replaced `{REDIRECT_URL}` value is attacker-influenceable (derived from the OAuth `return_url`) and lands inside a `<script>` string literal, so a single quote breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Music Assistant web origin — with the victim's freshly-minted auth token in scope.

### Location (line numbers as of `dev` @ `b86539f`)
- Sink: `music_assistant/controllers/webserver/controller.py:968-971`
  ```python

> **Status: already fixed.** Resolved by music-assistant/server#4544 (merged 2026-07-02), which removes the legacy `/imageproxy?provider=&path=` query-string form and its `_is_safe_imageproxy_request_path` validator. Filed here for the public record per maintainer request to split the coordinated private report (`GHSA-5cv4-xxvj-mpvc`) into one item per finding. No further action needed beyond confirming the fix reaches a release.

## Summary — unauthenticated arbitrary image-file read via legacy `/imageproxy` (CWE-22 / CWE-23)

The deprecated `/imageproxy?provider=&path=&size=&fmt=` route was registered on the **unauthenticated** stream server. Its safety check accepted empty-scheme (local) paths and performed no absolute-path or containment validation, so a remote, unauthenticated attacker could read arbitrary image-extension files anywhere on the host filesystem — and extract embedded cover-art from arbitrary media files.

## Impact

```
GET http://<host>:<stream-port>/imageproxy?provider=builtin&path=/absolute/path/to/file.png
```

returned the file bytes with **no authentication**. Scope was constrained (not unrestricted `/etc/passwd` read), which is why it was rated HIGH rathe

posts.excerpt:
## Environment

- **Home Assistant integration**: Music Assistant HA integration
- **Trigger**: `music_assistant.play_media` called simultaneously from two parallel Home Assistant script instances targeting two different `media_player` entities

## Description

When a Home Assistant automation calls a script in parallel for two kids' bedroom speakers, one or both speakers randomly stop playing in the middle of a track. The issue is intermittent — it does not happen every time, which makes it hard to reproduce deterministically.

This has been confirmed to occur with both **local library tracks** (`library://track/XX`) and **Spotify tracks/playlists**.

The same speakers work perfectly with a separate bedtime automation that uses an identical parallel structure calling `music_assistant.play_media` on both speakers. That automation has never exhibited this issue.

## Broken: Wake-up automation + script

**Automation** (mode: `single`):
```yaml
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: sensor.bedroom_speaker_turn_off_time

actions:
  - action: input_boolean.turn_off
    target:
      entity_id: input_boolean.kids_bedtime

  - parallel:
      - alias: kid_1
        action: script.wake_up_kid

I wanted to share a Home Assistant add-on I've been running alongside Music Assistant: **Metadata Remote** — a web-based audio tag editor that opens right inside the HA sidebar via ingress.

posts.excerpt:
Hi Team,

First of all, thank you for this amazing project! 

I would like to propose a clean, architectural solution for a persistent issue in the Media Browser (Browse view): the default sorting order.

## The Problem
Currently, when browsing local file-based systems (e.g., Local files, SMB shares), the default sort order is set to 'Original'. On Linux filesystems, 'Original' means the items are listed based on inodes/filesystem indexes, resulting in a completely scrambled, unreadable order. 

While users can manually switch the sort order to 'Alphabetical' on the UI, this setting is not persistent. Upon page refresh, pagination (loading more chunks), or navigating deeper into folders, the frontend reverts back to 'Original'. This makes browsing larger local directories highly frustrating.

### The Solution (Proposal)
Instead of trying to fix state persistence in the frontend or forcing a global default that might break streaming providers (like Spotify or Tidal, which rely on 'Original' to keep their curated order), **the default sort order should be handled at the Provider level.**

It would be amazing to have a dropdown setting within each Music Provider's config
posts.title: Provider-level default sort order for Media Browser

**Music Assistant version:** 2.9.3
**Provider:** Audiobookshelf (music provider)

### Symptom

The Audiobookshelf podcast sync (and the recommendations fetch) fail *wholesale* when a single podcast episode has an out-of-range year in its date:

```
WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.tasks] Background task Sync Audiobookshelf podcasts failed: year must be in 1..9999, not 10909
WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.music] Error while fetching recommendations from Audiobookshelf: year must be in 1..9999, not 40300
```

### Cause

An Audiobookshelf podcast had episodes whose date parsed to an out-of-range year (e.g. `10909`, `40300`). MA raises a `ValueError` building the `date`/`datetime`, and the exception propagates up and aborts the entire **Sync Audiobookshelf podcasts** background task (and the recommendations fetch). As a result **none** of the provider's podcasts/audiobooks import — not just the offending episode.

### Expected

An episode with an invalid / out-of-range date should still be **imported and shown — just with an empty / unset date** — and the sync should continue. A bad date value should degrade to "no date"; it should never skip the episode, and never abort th

posts.excerpt:
When listening to radio streams that provide artwork via the ICY `StreamUrl` field (e.g., album covers from radio station APIs), Music Assistant ignores this URL entirely. Instead, it always performs a MusicBrainz lookup to find artwork, which:

- Overrides the station-provided cover with a (sometimes different) MusicBrainz result
- Adds unnecessary API calls when the stream already provides the correct artwork
- Returns no artwork at all for talk radio programs, regional stations, or lesser-known tracks that MusicBrainz doesn't index

Many radio stations (Radio France, FIP, RMC, Catalunya Radio, etc.) expose high-quality, real-time artwork through their APIs. Tools like Node-RED or custom ICY proxies can inject this artwork into `StreamUrl`, but MA currently discards it.

Parse the `StreamUrl` field from ICY metadata in `_parse_icy_metadata()` and pass it to `_update_radio_stream_metadata()` as `image_url`.

posts.excerpt:
**Feature Request**

Currently, the "Default enqueue option for Track item(s)" in 
Settings → System → Player Queues only offers two options:

- Play (and keep queue)
- Play (and replace queue)

**What's missing**

There is no way to set **"Play next (and keep queue)"** as the 
default action for tracks. This option exists in the track 
context menu, but it cannot be saved as a permanent default.

**Expected behavior**

The same enqueue options available in the context menu should 
also be available as default settings in Player Queue settings, 
specifically:

- Play next (and keep queue)
- Play next (and replace queue)
- Add to queue

**Why this is useful**

When listening to music and browsing for the next song, most 
users want to queue it up as "play next" rather than 
immediately interrupting playback or adding it to the very end 
of a long queue. Having to right-click every single time is 
cumbersome.
posts.title: Add "Play next (and keep queue)" as default enqueue option for Track items

When a player has an empty queue, the Shuffle and Repeat buttons appear disabled. Since there is no "Play Shuffle" button, I need to start playing music and then enable the shuffle mode.

The issue is that I always start playing my favorite playlist with the same track (the first on the list) and there is no way to start with a random track when the player has an empty queue. I'd have to start playing the playlist, enable shuffle, and then start playing the playlist again.

I don't know if this is possible, but it would be very helpful to be able to set shuffle and repeat modes before playing any track. No matter if the queue is empty or not.

Or having a "Play Shuffle" button, but I think just having the shuffle and repeat buttons always enabled could be an easier solution?

### The problem

When using a Yamaha MusicCast receiver through Music Assistant with Sendspin/AirPlay as the preferred output protocol, advancing to the next track changes the parent MusicCast player's volume unexpectedly.

In this setup, the Music Assistant player `Living Room` is a Yamaha RX-V6A MusicCast player whose preferred output protocol is the Sendspin bridge for its AirPlay endpoint. On a normal `next` command, the Living Room volume dropped from 36% to 26% without any explicit volume command from Home Assistant or the user.

This looks like an AirPlay/Sendspin volume scale mismatch with the linked MusicCast parent:

- Music Assistant restarts the Sendspin/AirPlay bridge on track change.
- The bridge starts `cliraop` with `-volume 36`, copied from the parent MusicCast player's Music Assistant volume.
- The Yamaha AirPlay endpoint maps that to native MusicCast raw volume `43` out of `161`.
- Music Assistant's MusicCast provider reads that back as `int(43 / 161 * 100) == 26`.
- The parent player is then exposed as 26% volume.

Expected behavior: changing tracks through the Music Assistant queue should not change the native MusicCast parent player's volume when no explicit v

Problem

Currently, Music Assistant does not provide a native sleep timer functionality.
While this can be implemented through Home Assistant automations, it requires additional setup and is not very user-friendly for everyday usage.

A built-in sleep timer would significantly improve the user experience, especially for bedroom, children's room, or nighttime listening scenarios.

Proposed Solution

Add a native sleep timer feature to Music Assistant with options such as:

Stop playback after a selected duration
Optional fade-out before stopping
Per-player sleep timer support
Pause instead of stop (optional)
UI integration inside the player controls
Support for voice assistants / Assist

Example:

"Stop music in 30 minutes"
"Fade out music after 45 minutes"
Why This Would Be Useful

Many media platforms and audio systems already provide this feature because it is a very common use case.

Examples:

Spotify
Plex
Kodi
Traditional radio/alarm clock devices

Providing this directly in Music Assistant would:

improve usability
reduce automation complexity
make Music Assistant more accessible for non-technical users
improve mobile and voice assistant

The current logic of the (new) genre feature for local files is as follows
1. local nfo file
2. online sources such as MusicBrainz
3. propagated genre from tracks, if turned on in the "Local Files" provider

I personally do have my own genre matching and all my tracks therefore do have "my genres". I do not have local nfo files.

What happens is that if MusicBrainz can identify the artist properly, it will pull the genre (along with the bio and other metadata) from music brainz and I "dont want" MB's genre allocation.
I'm suggesting to change the logic to:
1. local nfo file
2. propagated genre from tracks, if turned on in the "Local Files" provider
3. online sources such as MusicBrainz
This would allow that you still get the bio and other items from the online metadata providers, but the genre would be propagated from the (local) tracks.

### How to get it

Check out the [sendspin-armv6](https://github.com/LeoLTM/sendspin-armv6) GitHub repository and follow the installation instructions in the `README.md` (run the `install.sh` script).

### Features

Plays music through available ALSA devices. No display, no controls, just audio output as a systemd daemon.
Will automatically try to reconnect if the connection to Music Assistant is lost.

### Prequisites

- Raspberry Pi Zero W with Raspberry Pi OS Lite
- USB Sound Card

### Why?

As an early adopter of Music Assistant, I had to try out the Sendspin protocol the moment it was released. It's great that there are existing clients for ESP32, Android etc. and projects like the Sendspin BT bridge.
As I had an "old" Raspberry Pi Zero W and a USB sound card laying around, I was thinking "why not use this as a Sendspin client?".

Unfortunately, the sendpspin-cli can't be run on the 1st gen Pi Zero, only the newer and more expensive Pi Zero 2W.
This is due to the fact that it relies on Python 3.12 which is not available for `ARMv6` devices like the Pi Zero W (The Zero 2W is `ARMv8`!).

posts.excerpt:
I have 2 older uPNP players which don't allow you to Pause live streams - they just ignore the Pause command when the source is a stream.  This means MA thinks it's paused the music and is in "paused" state, but the music is still playing.  In the Lyrion Music Server (aka Squeezebox) uPNP Bridge plugin this is solved by providing an option to replace Pause with Stop if the source is a stream.  The description is 


```
<live_pause>0 | 1</live_pause > default = 1

Some players will not pause when playing live streams (e.g.webradio). It’s correct that although you can buffer or “timeshift” livestream, in most case it does not make sense as gap with real time increases forever, at every pause. For such players, the bridge can commute LMS’ pause request into a stop (only when playing a livestream)
```


I wondered if it would be possible to add a similar option to the uPNP provider
posts.title: Add option to replace Pause with Stop for uPNP players with live streams

I've started working on a PoC implementing a mechanism that will allow users to block specific tracks or artists so they are automatically skipped during playback. This is particularly useful for provider auto-generated playlists, like radio-generated queues.

Before I finalize the implementation, I wanted to check if this aligns with the project vision and get your input.

Player Behavior:
- Blocked items are silently skipped
- If currently playing item gets blocked → immediate skip
- If no unblocked items remain in queue → graceful stop


**Implementation Plan**

1. Models

    Add blocked: bool = False attribute to:
    - Track dataclass
    - Artist dataclass

2. Server - Database & Controllers

    - Add blocked column to tracks and artists tables
    - Add set_blocked(item_id, blocked) method to TracksController and ArtistsController
    - Update queries to include blocked field

3. Server - API Commands

    Add to MusicController:
    - music/blocked/add_item - Block track or artist
    - music/blocked/remove_item - Unblock track or artist
    - music/blocked/items - List all blocked items

Using the `media_player.media_seek` action often resulted in the attribute not updating even though the track was advanced (or rewinded). When pausing the player the attribute seems to always be updated correctly.

What I think happens is at the point of enqeuing the next track the media position of the curently playing track is put into the attribute. Pausing and resuming the track results in the value being set correctly.

### The problem

When attempting to add a Jellyfin provider in Music Assistant, saving the configuration fails with an AssertionError in config_entries.py:213. The error occurs because the verify_ssl value, passed as a boolean (True or False), isn’t a string, which the to_raw() function expects. This prevents the provider from being added, and the process crashes before it can connect to the Jellyfin server.

### How to reproduce

Install Music Assistant v2.4.0 as a Home Assistant add-on.
Go to Settings > Music Providers in the Music Assistant UI.
Add a new Jellyfin provider with:
URL: http://[jellyfin-ip]:8096
Username: (your username)
Password: (your password)
Verify SSL: Check or uncheck the box (sets True or False)
Log Level: GLOBAL
Click Save.
The UI shows an "AssertionError," and the provider isn’t added.

### Music Providers

Jellyfin

N/A

I am trying to get music assistant to work with my google speakers on a VLAN, which was previously working but randomly stopped. Are there specific ports that MA requires? It seems like no combo of IGMP, Avahi, or UDP Relay works anymore. MA will discover and connect to the speakers, but it never starts playing. If I play a local file from home assistant to the same speaker, it works fine. Addititionally, if I remove all rules limiting any kind of traffic at all between VLANs, MA works but audio drops out after about 30 seconds? I was only able to test with plex but was unable to get any music to play all the way through. In the past I thought this was fixed by increasing the memory to HA but now there is more than enough RAM alloted to the VM, and the same issue appears in docker as well where there is no memory limit up to 128GB

posts.excerpt:
pacmd is handy to stream sound from one linux to another since it's in most repos and on desktops.
I use it to stream sound from Ubuntu VMs with Spotify to Rpi's connected to speakers all over the house.

The pacmd server runs on the Rpi and the client connects to it via:
pacmd load-module module-tunnel-sink server=SERVERIP:port

It creates a dummy sound card on the client machine.
Sound quality is good (PCM), it's reliable and it doesn't require any extra software besides what's in the distro already.

So Music assistant just needs to invoke the command above to connect to a remote pacmd server.

*On the Rpi side (or any computer connected to the speakers/amp) you run the command bellow to listen to the streams (or use the Pulsaudio extended GUI):
pactl load-module module-native-protocol-tcp port=PORT listen=SERVERIPADDRESS auth-ip-acl='127.0.0.1;CLIENTIP' auth-anonymous=1

SERVERIP=IP of Rpi player
CLIENTIP=IP of the MusicAssistant.
posts.title: Pulsaudio pacmd sound stream player support

It would be fantastic to have the ability to specify a local soundcard as an audio output for a player. This feature would effectively turn Music Assistant into a full-fledged open-source wired multi-room audio system.

To elaborate, I have a multi-room audio player from a company called CasaTunes, which is essentially a low-spec PC with two physical soundcards. Each output of these soundcards represents a zone (or room) and acts as an independent player. There are other companies employing the same approach while charging unreasonably high prices for it.

The idea of implementing local players would simply require the ability to specify the device and subdevice, for example:
```-a hw:1,0```

This enhancement would open up new possibilities for multi-room audio setups using wired connections, adding tremendous flexibility for users.

Hi! I'm using Music Assistant in Home Assistant to stream music to a receiver (Onkyo, DLNA). The MA volume slider controls the receiver's volume setting directly, but setting it below 30 is inaudible, and above 60 is dangerously loud. I've had users accidentally change the volume way too high with the slider, as they are accustomed to 0=not audible, 1=barely audible, 100=loud but not deadly. I didn't find any way to change the limits in MA or HA - HA Onkyo DLNA integration lets me set a maximum volume but the setting is not used by MA, and MA's volume normalization can be used to restrict the max volume, but then the receiver needs to be turned very high to hear anything, which is again dangerous when switching to another source. Apologies if this exists or doesn't belong in MA & thanks for the great app!

In summary: a per-output setting that changes what volumes 0 and 100 map to in the volume slider.

posts.excerpt:
As far as I can tell, Music Assistant currently uses ffmpeg's `loudnorm` filter to do loudness normalization. I'm unclear when that calculation is done (on demand? on import?), but it's a relatively cpu-heavy filter to run, and while the loudnorm filter's one-pass support for dynamic normalization (dynamic range compression, effectively) might be useful for radio or podcast streams, the filter is not always appropriate for local music files. (Note that for determining the integrated loudness of local files, ffmpeg's `ebur128` filter should run faster.)

But all of my music files contain pre-calculated "integrated" loudness adjustment information, stored either in the form of [ReplayGain 2.0 tags](https://wiki.hydrogenaud.io/index.php?title=ReplayGain_2.0_specification) or [Opus R128 Gain tags](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7845.html#section-5.2.1). It would be great if Music Assistant could retrieve and use this precalculated loudness normalization information, rather than do its own loudness calculations. (Note that the ReplayGain 2.0 tags use a reference level of -18 LUFS, while the Opus R128 tags use a reference level of -23 LUFS.)

Ideally, the ability to select whether
posts.title: Use ReplayGain (and Opus R128 Gain) tags for loudness normalization

posts.excerpt:
Once upon a time, the Google Home app supported casting the Android device device audio to a group of Chromecast devices - or Chromecast audio devices in my case. Then, Sonos sued Google, and they removed this functionality from their app. It still supports redirecting the device audio (or screen), but only to a single Chromecast devices, and no longer to a group.

My main use case is to cast audio from a Youtube music video playing in Firefox with an ad blocker, and casting that to more than one room at a  time, say a whole floor, or the whole house. I'm aware that in this case, the audio and video are out of sync, but that's not a concern at all since I'm not even looking at the screen, and the phone may even be locked while I listen.

It should be noted that even using all-Google software (say, Youtube app, Youtube Music app, or Chrome, and the Google Home app) there is no way to accomplish this, even to a single Chromecast device, let alone a group, as far as I know. The Youtube app can only cast to Chromecast video devices, not Chromecast audio. This is probably due to A/V sync reasons. And the Youtube Music app can only cast audio from specific media designated as audio,
posts.title: Support redirecting Android device audio

posts.excerpt:
Most AV receivers and renderer support 24 bit audio as Flac or WAV stream.
It would be great to have an option to choose between 16 and 24 bit output and processing to avoid loss in dynamic resolution when volume normalization is active.

@marcelveldt gave some very interesting insights in how audio is handled inside music assistant #1501 :

> All tracks are processed as raw pcm by Music Assistant internally. So everything you play will be first converted to just raw pcm in the sample rate and bit depth of the origin (unless flow mode is enabled) and the gain adjustment is done while extracting the raw source media so the pcm chunks we get into the streaming engine have the gain adjustment applied, that way there should be enough headroom withit the 16 or 24 bits sample rate. ... I settled on applying the correction gain while extracting the raw audio from its base codec. ...
> The final part in the chain is that MA sends either the raw pcm data to the player or encodes it into a codec of the user's choice, by default this is FLAC due to it being lossless while keeping a sane file size ... 

Currently there is an setting for normalization level (EBU) and output codec but no
posts.title: Add an option to choose between 16 or 24 bit processing and output

posts.excerpt:
ESPHome's Media Player currently seems to support only MP3 streams. MP3 is a lossy format, sound quality is degraded.
Music Assistant integration by default renders the audio streams in FLAC, which is a lossless format.
Would be nice to enable support in ESPHome for other codecs too:
- lossless FLAC
- uncompressed PCM up to 48k stereo
- open source OPUS (which is lossy, but way better than MP3)
- AAC (also lossy, but better than MP3 and OPUS)

Since only MP3 is supported, one needs to use other firmware than ESPHome, like squeezelite. The goal would be not to have to rely on third party stuff, but remain in the Home Assistant + ESPHome ecosystem.

Adding more codecs of course needs PSRAM for ESP32 (like WROVER module), which is not a problem as plenty of such modules are available. This just needs to be pointed out properly in the documentation.

Also requested in ESPHome FR repo: https://github.com/esphome/feature-requests/issues/1848
posts.title: Support more audio codecs, not just lossy MP3 - in ESPHome

Many Spotify users (including me) have configured and actively are using so-called music scrobbling. Scrobbling is recording the basic details about the song you just listen to like its title, artist or the name of the record and of course the timestamp. The most popular is last.fm but there are more like Libre.fm, ( based on gnu.fm open source) or ListenBrainz. 

Using this kind of service we can generate our database with statistics about the most frequently listened songs, records, and artists accessible for each day, month or any year in the past. This gives us unlimited possibilities to create our own dynamic playlists on Spotify or on other music providers (using tools like soundiiz.com). 

I can imagine having scrobbling stats kept (either locally and merged with my past activity or in the last.fm sent from HA in one batch) and can ask local AI to create and play my favourite songs **in the order which I want or shuffled exactly as I want** (say shuffling all songs from only one artist or only one mood or for example my favourite songs in May 2009). Alternatively the same could be achievable by sorting data in the Music Assistant UI, if we could create that kind of datab
posts.title: Support for last.fm service ( and music scrobbling in general)

posts.excerpt:
You can play an album --> the entire album (all tracks under it) is inserted and then played on the queue
You can play a playlist --> the entire playlist (all tracks under it) is inserted and then played on the queue

If you're browsing an album or a playlist and you click one of the tracks, the current default behavior is to play THAT track.
It will be inserted at the top of the queue and played. The existing items on the queue continue after that.

But what if you want to start playing an album/playlist from the track you selected. More like the behavior the Spotify app has.
There should be another enqueue option "Play from here", available when you're browsing an album or playlist listing.
If you select that, the entire playlist/album will be inserted in the queue from the position of the track you selected.
